description: Wire the FEAT-002 governance core into the control plane: admin API routes for the Directory (list/invite/suspend/reactivate/change-role members), the org-wide kill switch (freeze/unfreeze + status), and a read-only admin audit log endpoint — all gated by the RBAC capability matrix and emitting versioned admin audit rows with a correlation id. Enforce the kill switch and principal-state gate at the existing pre-model chokepoint so a frozen org or a suspended human fails closed on the NEXT gated action (not via a checklist). Every admin route re-derives the caller from the verified token (never the request), maps directory/govern errors to the existing HTTP codes, and writes an append-only admin audit entry for every state change. Depends on FEAT-002.
steps: In services/handlers/api.py, add an admin route group under a distinct path prefix (e.g. /admin/*) dispatched via the existing _match() pattern, ordered so specific paths resolve before parameterized ones (follow the /connectors/apps-before-/connectors/{id} precedent). Routes: GET /admin/directory (list members); POST /admin/directory/invites (invite a member — body: subject/email + role, defaulting scope to org); POST /admin/directory/{subject}/suspend; POST /admin/directory/{subject}/reactivate; PATCH /admin/directory/{subject} (change role); GET /admin/killswitch; POST /admin/killswitch (body {frozen:true|false}); GET /admin/audit (read-only, newest-first, from the org partition). Reuse _actor(event)/_principal(event); do NOT read the acting subject from the path or body.

Gate each admin route with directory.assert_can using the acting principal's membership (via the identity membership helper from FEAT-002) against the blueprint capability for that route: invite/change-role require invite_users/change roles per §4 (Owner/Admin); suspend/reactivate map to the offboarding controls (Owner/Admin/Security per terminate_computer semantics — use the closest matrix capability and document the choice in a WHY comment); killswitch freeze/unfreeze require an org-policy/security capability; GET /admin/audit requires read_audit_log (Owner/Admin/Security/Auditor). A caller lacking the capability gets 403 via the existing Escalation/PermissionError mapping.

For every admin state change, persist the change and then store an admin audit row from govern.admin_audit_event(...), threading a correlation id: generate one per request if the client did not supply an X-Correlation-Id header, and echo it back in the response so a UI can link an admin action to the resulting run evidence. Members, killswitch, and audit rows all live in the single DynamoDB table under keys added in FEAT-002; use store.transact_put where a change + its audit row must be atomic (mirror agent create), otherwise put the change then the audit row.

Thread the enforcement cut into the chokepoint: at the point in the request/agent-action path where policy.evaluate is consulted (and/or in _principal/_actor for human admin actions), call govern.assert_not_frozen(<killswitch row>) and govern.guard_principal(<membership>) so that (a) when the org is frozen every bot/connector action fails closed, and (b) a suspended human's in-flight work dies on its next gated action. Do this WITHOUT loosening any existing check and without adding a system-prompt rule (enforcement is code). If the natural chokepoint is in the orchestrator rather than api.py, add the guard call there and note it; keep the change minimal and covered by a test.

Add tests in tests/test_admin_api.py following the tests/test_gaps_api.py / tests/test_agents_api.py route-test pattern (monkeypatch api.Store to the moto table; build events with a verified-principal stub). Cover: an Owner can invite/suspend/reactivate/change-role and each writes an admin audit row carrying a correlationId; a Member (no invite_users capability) gets 403 on invite; GET /admin/audit is readable by an Auditor and forbidden to a plain Member; freezing the org via POST /admin/killswitch causes a subsequently gated action to fail closed (assert the frozen path returns the fail-closed error/status); a suspended human's next admin action returns 403 (pull-based). Assert the correlation id round-trips from the X-Correlation-Id header when supplied and is generated otherwise. Every test must fail if its guard is reverted.

Confirm the whole suite plus infra synth plus web build stay green (no new failures beyond the 3 pre-existing test_gaps_api.py ones), and that api.py still imports cleanly (no shadowed-module regression — tests/test_no_shadowed_modules.py must pass).
acceptance_criteria: Admin routes exist under /admin/* and each state-changing route writes an append-only admin audit row via govern.admin_audit_event with a correlationId
RBAC is enforced server-side: a caller without the required blueprint capability receives 403; an Auditor can read /admin/audit and a plain Member cannot
Freezing the org (POST /admin/killswitch {frozen:true}) makes a subsequently gated action fail closed; a suspended human's next admin action returns 403 (pull-based, no checklist)
The acting subject is always derived from the verified token, never from the request path/body/header (verified by a test that sends a mismatched subject in the path)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q shows the new tests passing with no NEW failures beyond the 3 pre-existing test_gaps_api.py ones; cd infra && npx cdk synth and cd web && npm run build stay green
verification: cd web && npm run build && test -f dist/index.html
findings:
Implemented in commit 27ee155. Edits: services/handlers/api.py (admin routes + helpers), services/handlers/orchestrator.py (enforcement cut), tests/test_admin_api.py (new). 

Routes added under /admin/* in _route(), specific-before-parameterized (invites and killswitch literals registered before /admin/directory/{subject}): GET/POST /admin/directory[/invites], POST /admin/directory/{subject}/suspend|reactivate, PATCH /admin/directory/{subject}, GET/POST /admin/killswitch, GET /admin/audit. Each admin handler re-derives the caller via _membership(store, event) = govern.guard_principal(identity.load_membership(...)); the {subject} in a path is only ever the target. Capability choices (documented in WHY comments): directory list + audit read = READ_AUDIT_LOG (Owner/Admin/Security/Auditor, plain Member forbidden); invite/reactivate/change-role = INVITE_USERS; suspend = TERMINATE_COMPUTER (closest offboarding control); killswitch status+set = CHANGE_ORG_POLICIES. State changes write an append-only govern.admin_audit_event row (versioned envelope, correlationId always present) via store.transact_put where atomic (invite: member+audit) or put+put (killswitch is an overwriteable single row, so transact_put's create-only condition can't be used on a re-freeze; suspend/reactivate/change-role do store.update then put the audit). X-Correlation-Id read case-insensitively via _header and echoed back in every state-changing response; absent -> admin_audit_event generates a corr_ id.

Enforcement cut: chose orchestrator._drive as the pre-model chokepoint. After the agent-active check it reads store.try_get(org_pk(owner_id),'KILLSWITCH') and calls govern.assert_not_frozen, failing the run closed (state FAILED, {'ok':false,'reason':'org frozen'}) before any tokens are spent. This covers 'a frozen org fails every bot/connector action closed on its next run/in-flight routine'. The suspended-human (pull-based) gate lives in api.py's _membership helper (govern.guard_principal on every admin request) so a suspended human's next admin action returns 403. store.owner_id == org_id today (the seam).

Multi-tenant seam note affecting tests: handler builds Store(principal.user_id) and org_id==user_id, so governance rows live under ORG#<caller-sub>. A non-owner caller therefore operates on their own org partition; tests seed MEMBER# rows under the caller's own subject to give them a role, and use org=OWNER when the Owner acts on another member of their org.

Verification: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -> 971 passed, 3 failed (the 3 PRE-EXISTING test_gaps_api.py toolchain-drift failures only; baseline was 955 passed + 16 new admin tests = 971). tests/test_admin_api.py (16) and tests/test_no_shadowed_modules.py pass. cd infra && npx cdk synth -> exit 0. cd web && npm run build -> exit 0, dist/index.html present. No new failures introduced.

=== REVIEW RESPONSE (commit 1d22d43, follow-up to the 2026-09-21 NEEDS_CHANGES review) ===
Addressed 6 in-scope issues; issue 7 left for a later slice as instructed. Full suite now 987 passed / 3 pre-existing failed; cdk synth + web build stay green.

Issue 1 (multi-tenant ownerId hazard) -- MADE HONEST (not a full rework). A full ownerId-by-orgId rework would touch the load-bearing Store invariant (ownerId == caller-sub) across the whole codebase, too large/risky for this slice. Instead the single-tenant limitation is now EXPLICIT and enforced by the data boundary rather than papered over: identity.load_membership carries a HONEST LIMITATION note spelling out that an invite writes MEMBER#<invitee> under the INVITER's org and the invitee's own Store keys on their OWN org, so a genuine second human cannot yet read a cross-org seat. The implicit-Owner fallback is documented as scoped to the caller's own org (never a silent cross-tenant read). Covered by tests that authenticate AS the invited subject: tests/test_identity.py::TestMembershipSeam::test_an_invitee_resolves_to_their_own_org_not_the_inviters and tests/test_admin_api.py::TestInvitedSeatIsSingleTenantHonest (invitee reads their own empty org, NOT the inviter's roster).

Issue 2 (assert_owner shadows RBAC) -- FIXED. Split token verification from the coarse owner-allowlist gate. api._principal now only verifies+caches the token; new api._authorize applies identity.assert_owner for non-/admin/* routes and SKIPS it for /admin/* (the _RBAC_ROUTE_PREFIX), so an invited Admin/Security/Billing/Auditor seat reaches the admin surface and RBAC (directory.assert_can) makes the finer decision. Token verify + Store ownerId isolation unchanged. Tests: TestRbacSeatReachesAdminUnderAllowlist (non-owner admin seat reaches /admin/* under a configured OWNER_SUBJECTS; a plain Member is still 403 via RBAC; non-admin routes still 401 under the allowlist).

Issue 3 (directory list leaks internal fields) -- FIXED. Added _member_view and _audit_view projections; _admin_list_members and _admin_audit (and every member response) now return only member-facing fields (subject/role/scope/scopeId/state/invitedBy/invitedAt for members; action/at/actor*/correlationId/before/after/detail/v for audit) -- no ownerId/pk/sk/gsi1pk/gsi1sk/timestamps. Tests: TestDirectoryDoesNotLeakInternalFields (asserts the exact key set and that internals are absent).

Issue 4 (killswitch GET/audit read store.owner_id, writes use actor.org_id) -- FIXED. Added _admin_org_id(event) derived from the verified principal; ALL admin reads and writes (list, roster, killswitch status/set, audit) now key on this one org id instead of store.owner_id. Test: TestOrgIdIsThreadedConsistently (status read reflects exactly what set wrote).

Issue 5 (invite input validation) -- FIXED. Added _parse_role -> A.ValidationError(400) on unknown/missing role (was a bare ValueError -> 500). _admin_invite now 400s on missing subject and on self-invite, and returns a clear 409 ('already has a seat') for a duplicate subject instead of an opaque transaction-cancelled Conflict. _admin_change_role uses _parse_role(body.get('role')) so a missing/invalid role is 400, not a KeyError/ValueError -> 500. Tests: TestInviteValidation.

Issue 6 (audit write atomicity) -- FIXED via audit-first ordering (documented why full atomicity isn't achievable). DynamoDB cannot mix a conditional Update of an existing MEMBER# row with a create-only Put of the audit row in one transaction the way agent-create's all-Puts transaction does, so with the current Store API full atomicity is not available for suspend/reactivate/change-role. New _apply_member_change writes the audit row BEFORE the state change, so a crash between them over-records (audit without state change) rather than under-records (state change with no trail) -- the safe direction for an append-only trail. Killswitch set likewise writes audit before the killswitch row. Invite remains fully atomic via transact_put (member+audit are both create-only Puts). Test: TestAuditIsWrittenFirst (monkeypatched Store.update crash leaves the audit row present and the member still ACTIVE).

Issue 7 (blueprint MVP follow-ups: ask-first policies/approval queue, usage/budget-cap routes, impersonation break-glass, connector-revoke-by-admin) -- INTENTIONALLY NOT IMPLEMENTED this slice, per the orchestrator briefing/review marking them deliberate follow-ups.
